# EmasCare: Teman Siang Project Plan

**Scope update (21 Oct 2026):** Tanya Dulu is a future feature, excluded from the current MVP and prototype builds. The current elder home has three main actions: Saya OK, Jom Keluar, and Minta Teman.

**Confirmed reward update (21 Oct 2026):** eligible completed activities/helping sessions earn coins for participating elders and helpers. The monthly 300-coin/four-session award is superseded. Coin values, the detailed eligibility/attendance rules and exact response JSON remain pending; see the EmasCare Coins section.

## Executive summary

EmasCare should be built as a module inside the Sime Darby Property (SDP) App that gives older parents who are home alone on weekdays a daily check-in, a reason and a companion to go out, and simple access information, with company provided by neighbours who are free in the daytime and thanked with SDP-only coins. We recommend SDP pilot it for 12 weeks in City of Elmina, starting with the multigenerational households of Ilham Residence.

The target group is large and overlooked. About 74% of Malaysian elders live with a child and only about 6% live alone, yet most services are designed for those living alone. With female labour force participation at a record 69% in Selangor, many of these parents spend 8am to 7pm alone. One in seven older Malaysians falls each year, a third report poor social support, and people aged 61 and above bear 27.9% of online-fraud losses.

The solution follows the **SIANG framework**: **S**aya OK (daily check-in), **I**nvite out (weekday activities), **A**ccess notes (simple, coordinator-updated access information), **N**eighbour companion (vetted daytime helpers in recurring pairs) and **G**ain & give back (coins after eligible completed activities/helping sessions for elders and helpers, accumulated toward SDP voucher redemption). The headline AI is a multilingual voice assistant. The MVP runs entirely in the SDP App, and WhatsApp and full route mapping are deferred to Phase 2\.

The plan's weakest points are evidence and validation. Before the finale, the team must show through interviews, a Daytime Availability Survey and usability tests that elders want company and outings, accept a self-controlled check-in, and that enough residents are free and willing to help.

## Background & data

### Malaysia is ageing fast

| Indicator | Value | Source |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Population aged 65+ | **8.4% (2026)**, up from 8.0% in 2025 | DOSM Current Population Estimates 2026 |
| States with "ageing" status (65+ \> 7%) | **12 states**; Perak highest at 10.8% | DOSM 2026 |
| Aged 60+ | \~4.1m (12%) in 2025 → 4.8m (13.3%) by 2030 → \~1 in 5 by 2050 | KPWKM via The Vibes, Jun 2026 |
| Old-age dependency ratio | 11.4 → 11.9 in one year | DOSM 2026 |
| "Aged nation" (65+ ≥ 14%) | \~2043–2048, depending on source | theSun 2025; KPWKM |

### Most elders live *with* family, but alone on weekdays

| Indicator | Value | Source |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Elders living alone | **6.18%** | HIES 2009 (Mohd et al., 2016\) |
| Elders living with a child | **\~74%** (64.17% with an adult child) | HIES 2009 |
| Malaysians in multigenerational homes | \~85% | MARS Wave 2 (SWRC UM), The Edge, Sep 2026 |
| Female labour force participation | **56.6% (record, Q4 2025); Selangor 69.0%** | DOSM LFS, Feb 2026 |
| Adults aged 60+ using the internet | **92.3% (2025)** | DOSM ICT Survey 2025 |

Japan calls this situation **日中独居 *nicchū dokkyo*** ("daytime living alone"). Daytime-alone elders show **lower motor function, higher fall risk and loss of household roles** compared with full-time solitary elders (Uehara et al., Kagoshima Univ., 2018).

### Sime Darby Property context

- **Purpose:** "to be a *Value Multiplier* for people, businesses, economies and the planet". It has 26 townships and asks how to help families "long after the keys are handed over".  
- **Already designs for this family:**  
  - Ilham Residence (City of Elmina, 2019), a multi-generational pilot with ramped, senior-ready ground-floor units  
  - Serenia Parkview and Nilai Impian, both multigenerational  
  - GMD Datuk Seri Azmir Merican says SDP designs from "**a senior's typical day**"  
- **Has the channels:** the Sime Darby Property App (owner accounts, household nominees, events, photo defect reports, **voucher wallet and mall module**) and malls (Elmina Lakeside, KL East, KLGCC) for reward redemption.  
- **Hackathon terms:** People track; judged on Relevant, Impactful, Innovative, Feasible, Scalable and Evidence based.

## Problem & research

### Problem statement

> **In SDP townships, older parents who live with working children spend most weekdays alone. No one would notice for hours if something went wrong. They rarely go out because they lack company and don't know whether the route will work for them. Their children worry from the office but can't help until evening.**

### Root causes

![Figure 1. Root causes of the problem][image1]

*Figure 1\. Root causes of the problem*

### Evidence for each part of the problem

| Problem part | Evidence | Confidence |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Large group is daytime-alone | 74% co-reside with a child; record female LFPR | Medium: co-residence data is from 2009, and daytime-alone hours aren't measured in Malaysia |
| Falls go unnoticed | 14.3% of 60+ fall yearly; Japanese daytime-alone elders show higher fall risk | Medium |
| Isolation → scams | 61+ bear 27.9% of fraud losses; JKM DG links isolation to scams (Oct 2026\) | High |
| Elders stay in because of access and company | Klang Valley mobility study: "continued need for help to reach destinations"; pedestrian infrastructure failures | Medium: for wheelchair users; not yet shown for walker or stick users |
| Children worry and lose work time | Working caregivers take unpaid leave or quit; 32.2% caregiver burden | Medium |
| Elders *want* company and outings | **No local evidence yet** | Not yet: must validate (see Riskiest assumptions) |

### Existing solutions and the gap

| Existing | What it does | Gap for daytime-alone elders |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| JKM Khidmat Bantu di Rumah | Stipended volunteers visit elders/OKU (1:4 ratio, RM400/month) | Targets those living alone or in need; not township-based; no outings |
| PAWE senior activity centres | Activities, digital literacy | Members struggle with transport and access |
| Rukun Tetangga / KRT / RA | Neighbourhood committees; some run senior groups | No digital coordination; ad hoc |
| SOS / fall-detector devices (some KRTs) | Emergency alert | Detects emergencies only; no company, no reason to go out |
| Google Maps, Wheelmap, IncluCity by NakSeni | Place-level accessibility | No route status, no repair owner, no companion |
| GrabAssist | Assisted rides (Klang Valley) | Paid trips outside the township; no daily presence |
| Homage Malaysia / agencies | Paid care RM30–55/hr | Too costly for daily companionship; overkill for low-need elders |
| Family WhatsApp calls | Ad hoc check-ins | Interrupts work; nothing if the elder doesn't answer |
| **SDP App** | Owner services, defects, vouchers | No elder or community features |

**Gap:** no service combines *daily notice \+ company \+ a safe way out* during working hours, delivered where these families already are (their township and SDP App).

## Solution

### The SIANG framework

*Siang* means "daytime" in Malay. Five pillars, each tied to a root cause:

| Pillar | What | Root cause addressed |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **S: Saya OK** (safe check-in) | Daily tap (or voice reply) in the SDP App, or a call from a phone buddy; escalation to the family if missed; "I want to talk" option | No one would notice |
| **I: Invite out** | Weekday activity calendar: tai chi in Central Park, surau/temple talks, PAWE, community garden, mall walking | No reason to go out |
| **A: Access notes** (MVP) | Each activity on the calendar shows an **access note** (step-free? toilet? benches? walk time) \+ **one live status line** the coordinator can toggle ("Block C lift under repair, use ramp \+3 min"); plain "report a problem" button. *Full route map, routing and AI photo triage are Phase 2* | Unknown route conditions |
| **N: Neighbour companion** | **Teman Siang helpers**: verified residents who are home in the daytime (students, homemakers, retirees, shift/remote workers) walk with, sit with, or help the elder with their phone; recurring pairs | No companion; traditional volunteers are scarce |
| **G: Gain & give back** | **Elders and helpers earn coins after each eligible completed activity/helping session**, accumulate them in their own wallets, and redeem vouchers; exact rates remain pending; family give-back and **light gamification** encourage participation | Supply problem; elders losing roles; stigma of "receiving" |

Cross-cutting: privacy by design under the PDPA; clear task boundaries for helpers; place and helper reporting. **Tanya Dulu** scam questions and AI assistance are future work, outside the current MVP.

**Priority for the hackathon:** S, I, N and G are the core demo. A is built as simple **access notes on activities**, about 1–2 days of work, with one live status change in the demo.

### Users and roles

| Role | Who | Main surface |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Elder (primary) | Daytime-alone parent, 60+ | Simple mode in the SDP App; phone-buddy call as fallback |
| Family (second user) | Working adult child, SDP owner-account holder | SDP App module |
| **Teman Siang helper** (daytime) | Residents free on weekdays: university students, homemakers, active retirees, shift/remote workers | Helper mode in SDP App |
| Weekend helper | Working adults (incl. family members) | Helper mode in SDP App |
| Coordinator | RA/KRT member \+ SDP community staff | Web dashboard |
| Asset owners | SDP township team, council (MBSA), JMB | Report inbox / email / SISPAA prefill |

### System architecture

![Figure 2. System architecture (MVP)][image2]

*Figure 2\. System architecture (MVP)*

**Design principles:**

1. **Module, not new app.** The family-facing part lives in the SDP App and reuses login and household nominees. The elder gets a simple-mode view in the same app. **Everything in the MVP runs inside the SDP App.**  
2. **Humans decide, AI assists.** AI never certifies a route as safe, never chooses a helper, never infers health.  
3. **Least data.** "Home alone" status and addresses are never exposed. Location is shared only during an active session.  
4. **A human fallback, not another channel.** Elders who can't use the app get a scheduled call from a phone buddy or the coordinator, who records the check-in for them. WhatsApp is Phase 2\.

The windows are illustrative; each elder sets their own times. This is not an emergency service, and the UI always shows 999\.

**Flow C: barrier report, re-route and fix** *(Phase 2, not in the hackathon MVP. In the MVP a coordinator sets the status manually.)*

![Figure 5. Flow C: barrier report (Phase 2)][image5]

*Figure 5\. Flow C: barrier report (Phase 2\)*

**Flow D: a recurring companion's contribution and rewards**

1. Aisyah, 21, a UM student living in Elmina, sets her availability: Tue/Thu 9am–12pm.  
2. The coordinator proposes a **regular pairing**: "Be Mr Tan's Teman Siang on Tuesdays, starting with tai chi at Central Park. 中文/BM." There is no open job feed to grab tasks from.  
3. Aisyah and Mr Tan meet with the coordinator (or by video), and both agree to a **4-week trial**.  
4. Each Tuesday she checks in at the meeting point; after each session both confirm.  
5. After each eligible verified completion, Aisyah and any eligible elder participant receive the configured coins in their own wallets. Their exact reward values still need agreement. Her factual impact card can read "4 Tuesdays with Mr Tan."
6. Once either participant has enough coins, they can redeem a voucher. The MVP issues mock vouchers; actual merchant redemption and any later transfer or milestone features require separate implementation.

**Flow E: weekend give-back.** Daniel (the working son) joins the Saturday Central Park walk with other elders. His household's **give-back milestone** counter goes up, and his dad sees "Your son helped Puan Rohani today."

### Teman Siang helpers: invite people who are home in the daytime

**Why not rely on volunteers:** traditional volunteers are scarce on weekdays (KampungKakis's main problem was volunteer time), and good intentions don't reliably turn into action (82.7% of Nanjing students said they'd join a time bank, but far fewer actually did). So EmasCare **invites residents who are already at home or free in the daytime** and **rewards them** for helping.

**Who is free on weekday daytime (national scale):**

| Pool | Size (Malaysia) | Typical free window (hypothesis to test) | Fit |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Homemakers (housework/family, outside labour force) | ≈ **3.08m** (43.3% of 7.11m) | \~8:30am–12:30pm, after school drop-off | Walks, sit-with-me, groceries; often same-gender/language matches |
| Students in schooling/training | ≈ **2.87m** (40.3% of 7.11m); **1.26m** in higher education | Timetable gaps; semester breaks | Phone/tech help, walks, activity buddies; intergenerational |
| Active "young-old" retirees (65+, not in labour-force stats) | ≈ **2.9m** aged 65+ | Mornings | Walking buddies, phone buddies; peers |
| Retired / other outside labour force (15–64) | ≈ 1.17m | Flexible | All light tasks |
| Shift workers, remote/hybrid workers, gig workers | Not quantified | Off-shift days, lunch hours | Short sessions, phone buddy |

Sources: DOSM Labour Force June 2026; DOSM population 2026; MOHE enrolment 31 Dec 2025\.

**Helper tiers (safety scales with access):**

| Tier | Who | Can do | Requirements |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| T1 Phone buddy | Any verified SDP household member 18+ | Scheduled calls, tech help by phone or video | ID via SDP account, 30-min online module |
| T2 Public-space companion | T1 \+ police clearance | Walk-with-me, activity buddy, sit-with-me in public places | Police clearance (PDRM/MyEG, with consent), 2-hour training, 2 supervised sessions |
| T3 Regular companion | T2 \+ 5 good sessions \+ coordinator approval | Recurring pairing; meet at the door; carry groceries home (doorstep only) | Coordinator review; refresher training |

**Lesson from Papa (US "grandkids on demand"):** paying companions scaled supply, but Bloomberg found dozens of harassment/assault allegations across 1.6m+ visits. Insurers dropped Papa, and it had to add multi-source vetting, identity verification, number anonymisation, an emergency button and visit monitoring. **EmasCare builds those in from day one** (see risk R1).

### EmasCare Coins: rewards after eligible completed contributions

**Confirmed decision (21 Oct 2026):** elders and helpers earn coins after each eligible completed activity or helping session. Their balances accumulate and can be used for voucher redemption. This replaces the earlier fixed monthly 300-coin award and its four-session threshold.

**Exact coin values and eligibility details are still pending.** Do not treat the former 300/150-coin monthly figures, RM conversion, milestone bonuses or related budget estimates as approved rates.

| Participant / event | Intended reward behavior | Still to agree |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Elder participates in an eligible community activity | Credit the elder after verified participation | Attendance verification and activity reward amount |
| Helper completes an eligible helping session | Credit the helper after the session meets its confirmation requirements | Per-task eligibility and helper reward amount |
| Elder/helper is an eligible participant in a completed activity/helping session | Each eligible beneficiary receives their own configured reward once | Participant eligibility and role-specific values; equal values are not assumed |
| Elder contributes by helping or teaching | Can qualify as a contributor under the same per-completion model | Supported contribution types and verification |
| Elder or helper accumulates enough coins | Redeem from their own wallet; backend deducts the voucher price and records the voucher | Confirm reward rates; the two-day demo retains its illustrative 100-coin mock voucher |

**How the reward flow works:**

1. The underlying activity/helping event is completed and verified. Accompanied sessions retain separate elder/helper confirmations.
2. The backend applies the agreed event/participant rule and credits each eligible participant's wallet.
3. The immutable ledger records the source completion, beneficiary, rule/rate and server time. Repeating the same confirmation or retry does not earn another reward.
4. A genuinely new eligible completion can add more coins. There is no month-end wait or minimum number of sessions for a monthly award.
5. When the user has sufficient balance, voucher redemption debits the coins once and adds the issued voucher to My Vouchers.

An activity attended during a companion session must not be credited twice to the same participant under separate activity/session representations. Standalone activity attendance needs an agreed verification path. Requested, cancelled or partly confirmed sessions do not qualify. Saya OK remains outside the confirmed activity/help reward scope.

Recurring pairings remain part of the companionship design. The reward change does not introduce an open job feed or change the coordinator's pairing role.

**Wallet and redemption scope:**

- Both elders and helpers can hold earned demo coins and redeem their own mock vouchers.
- The product vision links redemption to participating SDP malls, township merchants, events and facilities; actual acceptance and merchant settlement remain future integration work.
- The current MVP has no coin purchase, cash-out, household transfer, donation, expiry or milestone-bonus implementation.
- Coin values, reward coverage and event volume must be agreed before estimating the funding pool. The previous monthly reward budget is obsolete.

**Funding and value to SDP (proposed):** SDP community/marketing funding and participating-merchant offers could support redemption. The intended benefits remain resident participation, app engagement, community contribution and merchant visits. Funding arrangements require pilot agreement.

**API handoff:** the separately supplied proposed v1 contract's monthly eligibility/award functions and helper-only wallet/redemption permissions are superseded. Revise them for per-completion rewards and both roles before implementation. Exact response JSON remains unconfirmed.

### Daytime Availability Census (the research built into sign-up)

Helper sign-up doubles as research on **how many people are free in the daytime, and when**:

- **Sign-up asks:** free days and time blocks (e.g. Mon–Fri, 2-hour blocks), languages, tasks they're comfortable with, preferred reward (coins / certificate / just helping), and role (student / homemaker / retiree / shift worker / other).  
- **Output:** an **anonymised supply heatmap per township** (day × time block × role), compared with elder demand (requested times).  
  - It shows SDP and researchers where supply and demand don't overlap, e.g. "Wed 2–4pm: 12 requests, 3 helpers".  
  - It guides recruitment: "we need more homemakers on Wed afternoons".  
- **Before the pitch:** run the same questions as a quick survey (Google Form) in Elmina/Subang community Facebook and WhatsApp groups and among UM students (target n ≥ 50\) to get a **first real number**: % of respondents free ≥2 hrs on weekdays, and their usual windows.  
- **Privacy:** availability reveals who is home, so **publish aggregates only** (minimum cell size ≥5 people), never individuals' home times.

### Pilot service blueprint (12 weeks, City of Elmina)

| Layer | Weeks 1–2 | Weeks 3–10 | Weeks 11–12 |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Elders & families | Recruit 30–50 via Ilham Residence and RA; consent; set check-in times | Daily check-ins, 2 outings per week | Exit interviews; before/after measures |
| Teman Siang helpers | Recruit 20–30 (students, homemakers, retirees) via RA, school-parent groups, UM/nearby campuses; availability census; tiered onboarding \+ police clearance for T2+ | Recurring pairs; rewards after eligible verified completions; monthly debrief | Retention survey; availability heatmap report |
| Coordinators | 1 RA lead \+ 1 SDP community officer | Daily dashboard check (15 min) | Playbook write-up |
| Access notes | Team site visit: notes for \~5 activity places (MVP) → staff audit adds more | Coordinator updates live status; "report a problem" inbox | Note accuracy spot-check |
| SDP | App module \+ coin/voucher pool \+ merchant onboarding | Weekly KPI report | Go / no-go for more townships |

## UI/UX and tech stack

### UX principles (with evidence)

| Principle | Why (evidence) | How |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Simple mode for elders** | Usability and perceived usefulness drive (non-)adoption; intention ≠ behaviour (Coventry & Briggs 2016\) | Home \= 3 big buttons: **Saya OK · Jom Keluar · Minta Teman**. ≤3 taps per task. Tanya Dulu is reserved for a future release. |
| **Readable and tappable** | Age-related vision and dexterity changes; WCAG 2.2 | Body text ≥18–20 pt, scales with system font; contrast ≥7:1 for key text (WCAG AAA); targets ≥48×48 dp; icon \+ text label; no swipe-only actions; no time-outs |
| **Voice-first option** | Literacy and typing barriers; Malay, dialects, code-switching | Hold-to-talk in BM/EN/中文/Tamil; AI turns speech into a structured request, then reads it back for confirmation |
| **Their language** | Multilingual households; PLOS ONE finds lower volunteering odds among Chinese Malaysians | BM, EN, 中文, Tamil; match helpers by language |
| **Not surveillance** | FPF 2026: "look-ins" feel like surveillance; \~79% of elders reject caregivers consenting for them | Elder sets check-in times and who sees what; family sees *daily status*, never location or camera; elder can pause or withdraw |
| **Dignity framing** | Stigma about "being old" (walking-stick *malu*); loss of roles | Language of activity ("Jom keluar", "Teman"), not "lonely/frail"; elders can be helpers too |
| **Human fallback** | Not every elder will use an app, even with 92.3% online | Phone buddy / coordinator calls and records the check-in or request for the elder; family can act as proxy in the app (WhatsApp channel \= Phase 2\) |
| **Mascot optional** | Untested whether elders find it respectful | A/B test with and without the dog guide in W3 usability tests |
| **Trust signals** | About half of users can't tell if apps respect privacy (FPF) | Plain-language privacy card; "verified by SDP" badge; helper photo, name and tier badge shown only after match |

**Four surfaces:**

- Elder simple mode  
- Family view (SDP App module)  
- Helper mode (availability, task cards with meeting point only, coin wallet)  
- Coordinator web dashboard (check-in exceptions, requests, reports)

### Recommended tech stack

| Layer | Choice | Why | Alternative |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Mobile app | **Flutter** | One codebase for iOS/Android; strong accessibility support (semantics, text scaling); can be embedded as a module in an existing native app | React Native |
| Coordinator dashboard | Flutter Web or Next.js | Reuse code / fast admin UI | n/a |
| Auth | Firebase Auth (demo) → **SDP App SSO** (pilot) | Household roles come from SDP nominees | n/a |
| Operational DB | Cloud Firestore | Real-time updates for check-ins and requests; offline cache | Supabase Postgres |
| Access notes (MVP) | **Firestore `places` collection** with access fields \+ `liveStatus`; no routing engine | Buildable in 1–2 days; no geo infrastructure | n/a |
| Geo \+ routing (Phase 2\) | PostGIS \+ pgRouting on Cloud Run | Custom weights per mobility profile; OSM export | GraphHopper custom profiles |
| Map rendering | **MVP: a static map image per place \+ "Open in Google Maps" deep link** (walking directions). Phase 2: MapLibre \+ OSM with own data layer | Zero map SDK work for the demo | Google Maps SDK |
| Serverless logic | Cloud Functions / Cloud Run \+ Cloud Scheduler | Check-in timers and escalations | n/a |
| Notifications | **MVP: FCM push inside the SDP App only.** Phase 2: WhatsApp Business Platform (SDP-owned number) and SMS for elders who don't open apps | Zero third-party setup for the demo | n/a |
| AI | Gemini Flash-class via Vertex AI / Gemini API; ILMU evaluated for production | See the AI section | n/a |
| Storage | Cloud Storage (blurred images only) | n/a | n/a |
| Observability | Audit log of every data access by role | PDPA accountability | n/a |
| Hosting region | Prefer a Malaysian region if available, else Singapore with a Transfer Impact Assessment | PDPA s129 cross-border rules | n/a |

**Demo vs pilot:** the hackathon demo can run fully on Firebase, with access notes as plain Firestore documents (no map or routing engine). The pilot adds SDP SSO, police-clearance workflow and voucher-wallet integration. WhatsApp is considered only after the pilot shows that the in-app and phone-buddy channels miss some elders.

### Gamification: thin layer now, no game economy

**Decision:** include it in the MVP, but only as a thin layer on events the system already tracks (outings, walks, weekend sign-ups). It adds roughly 2–3 days of build, not a new subsystem.

**Evidence:**

- A 2026 systematic review (Hong & Choi, *Gerontechnology*; 75 studies, adults 55+) finds gamification **generally improves engagement and adherence** in older adults. Effects on health and behaviour are mixed. Usability, enjoyment and digital familiarity matter.  
- A 2025 systematic review (Chen et al., *JMIR Aging*; 8 studies, 1,454 participants) found the most-used elements were **goals and rewards, then challenges and collaboration**. Social features and a **support partner** improved step counts. Long-term effects are unproven.  
- For volunteers, a randomised study (57 Swedish volunteers) found **badges made no difference** where intrinsic motivation is already high. Design around **purpose, autonomy and impact** instead.  
- Motivation-crowding research: small rewards can reduce goodwill (risk R5).

**What we build (by user):**

| User | Game element | Why | What we avoid |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Elder | **Weekly outing goal** (a ring that fills: "2 of 2 outings this week") \+ coins for eligible verified activity/help participation \+ optional mascot | Progress, participation and appreciation; coin rates still need agreement | Streaks that "break", guilt messages, points for check-ins (never gamify the safety signal) |
| Elder \+ family | **Shared progress / cheer**: the son sees "Dad went to tai chi" and taps a clap; Dad sees the cheer | Collaboration \+ support partner \= strongest evidence | Comparing elders with each other |
| Helper | **Impact story cards** from confirmed sessions \+ coins after each eligible verified helping completion; wallet and voucher redemption | Factual impact and appreciation; coin rates still need agreement | Generic badge collections, individual leaderboards |
| Household | **Family give-back counter** (weekend helping by any family member) | Reciprocity, "families helping families" | Turning help into a transaction |
| Township | **Collective goal** ("Elmina this month: 312 of 500 walks together") | Collaboration, community pride, SDP PR value | Ranking townships or people |

**Out of scope (would make it too big):** levels, XP economies, leaderboards, avatars or shops, tradable tokens, and any cash value beyond capped SDP mall vouchers.

### One app: everything in the SDP App (MVP), WhatsApp later

**Decision (16 Oct 2026):** the MVP runs **entirely inside the SDP App**. There is no WhatsApp integration and no WhatsApp mock.

- **Elder:** "Simple mode" view of the SDP App module, with the 3 main buttons, check-in, voice and activity cards.
- **Family:** the same module; the parent is added as a **household nominee** (an existing SDP App feature). In the demo, the family types the parent's details. No one-time-code verification (pilot-phase security).  
- **Helpers:** "Helper mode" in the same app. **Coordinator:** a web dashboard.  
- **Notifications:** SDP App push only.  
- **Elders who won't use an app:** the human fallback. A phone buddy or the coordinator calls at the check-in time and records "OK" for them, and the family can book on their behalf.

**Why:**

- No dependency on Meta (business verification, template approval, per-message cost, AI-chatbot policy), so it fits the 4-week build.  
- One codebase, one login, one data store. All value stays in the SDP ecosystem by design.  
- A simpler privacy story: no data passing through a third-party messaging platform.

**Phase 2 (roadmap slide only): WhatsApp as the "doorbell".**

- An SDP-owned verified WhatsApp Business number sends only structured messages (morning "Saya OK?" buttons, reminders), each linking back into the app ("WhatsApp is the doorbell, the SDP App is the house").  
- Meta's ban on general-purpose AI chatbots (since 15 Jan 2026\) means the voice AI stays in the app either way.  
- Trigger for Phase 2: pilot data shows a meaningful share of elders missing app check-ins.

### Build spec: "A" as Access Notes (simple system first)

**Goal:** answer the elder's real question, *"Can I get there and manage there today?"*, without a map engine. Everything is plain data plus one toggle.

**Data model (Firestore):**

places/{placeId}

  name:            "Central Park, Gate B (tai chi)"

  township:        "City of Elmina"

  photo:           gs://.../gateB.jpg          // from the team's site visit

  walkFrom:        { "Ilham Residence": 6 }    // minutes, measured on site

  stepFree:        true

  accessibleToilet:{ available: true, distanceM: 50 }

  seating:         true                        // benches / rest spots

  shade:           "partial"                   // none | partial | covered

  dropOff:         true                        // car/e-hailing drop-off point

  notes\_bm / notes\_en / notes\_zh: "Masuk ikut pintu B, laluan rata..."

  liveStatus:      { level: "warning", text: "Lif Blok C rosak, guna laluan tanjakan (+3 min)",

                     setBy: "coordinator", updatedAt: ts, expiresAt: ts }

  mapsUrl:         "https\://maps.google.com/?q=..."   // deep link, walking mode

  owner:           "SDP" | "MBSA" | "unknown"          // for reports (manual in MVP)

activities/{activityId}  \-\> placeId, day, time, title, language   // links I-pillar to A

reports/{reportId}       \-\> placeId?, text, photo?, createdBy, status: new|seen|done

**Screens (3 small ones):**

1. **Activity card (elder):** title \+ time \+ **access icons** (step-free, toilet 50 m, benches, 6 min walk) \+ the **live status banner** if set \+ "Open in Google Maps" \+ the existing "Jom / Minta Teman" buttons. Teman voice reads the note aloud.  
2. **Report a problem (anyone):** text or photo, optional place picker, sent to the coordinator inbox. No AI.  
3. **Coordinator dashboard tab:** list of places; set or clear a live status (warning/closed/OK \+ short text \+ expiry); see new reports, mark "seen/done".

**Logic (all simple):**

- Cloud Function: when `liveStatus.expiresAt` passes, clear it automatically, so stale warnings don't linger.  
- When a status is set on a place, push a notification to elders (and their helpers) with an activity there in the next 24 h: "Heads up: …".  
- No routing, no geo queries, no AI in A.

**Data collection (1 site visit, \~half a day):** for each of \~5 places (Central Park gate, Elmina Lakeside Mall entrance, clinic, surau/temple, community hall), take photos, count walk minutes from Ilham Residence, and check toilet, benches, steps and shade against the MS 1184 universal design checklist (step-free, ramp ≤1:12, door ≥800 mm). Use Google Street View to prepare beforehand.

**Effort estimate:**

| Task | Time |
| :---- | :---- |
| Firestore schema \+ seed 5 places | 0.5 day |
| Activity card with access icons \+ status banner (Flutter) | 0.5 day |
| Coordinator status toggle \+ reports inbox | 0.5 day |
| Expiry function \+ "heads up" push | 0.5 day |
| Site visit \+ data entry | 0.5 day |
| **Total** | **\~2.5 days (1 person)** |

**Demo moment (30 seconds):** the coordinator taps "Lift at Block C under repair". Mr Tan's tai chi card instantly shows the warning. Teman reads it aloud in 中文, and Kak Lina (his helper) gets the same heads-up.

**Phase 2 upgrade path (pitch slide only):**

- Segment-level route mapping  
- Mobility-profile routing (PostGIS/pgRouting)  
- AI photo triage of reports  
- Automatic routing to the responsible owner (SDP/MBSA via SISPAA)  
- Freshness metric  
- OSM export

The `places` schema stays compatible: Phase 2 adds `segments` without changing what's built now.

## AI: what, which model, why

### Headline AI: "Teman" voice assistant (in the SDP App)

Elders can **speak instead of tap or type**, in BM, English, 中文, Tamil or a mix ("Saya nak pergi tai chi esok, ada kawan tak?", meaning "I want to go to tai chi tomorrow, is anyone free to come?"). AI turns speech into a structured action, **reads it back**, and the elder confirms.

Why voice is the headline:

- Typing and app navigation are the main barriers for elders, even though 92.3% of over-60s are online.  
- Malaysian elders code-switch, and voice removes the language and literacy burden.  
- It fits the hackathon's "technology, data or AI" requirement with a clear human benefit.

### Where AI is used, pillar by pillar

| SIANG pillar | AI use | Example | MVP? | Guardrail |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **S**: Saya OK | Understand voice or free-text check-in replies and **flag concern words** to the coordinator | "OK, tapi pening sikit" (OK, but a bit dizzy) → "OK \+ concern" → coordinator calls | Yes | Flags for a human; **no diagnosis**; never replaces the check-in button |
| **I**: Invite out | Read today's activities aloud (TTS) in the elder's language; simple suggestions from past preferences | "Today: tai chi 10am, Kak Lina is going" | Yes (read-aloud) | Suggestions only |
| **A**: Access notes | None in the MVP; **photo triage of barrier reports in Phase 2** | n/a | No (Phase 2\) | Human verifies; never certifies a route as safe |
| **N**: Neighbour companion | **Voice → booking**: extract activity, day, time, task type, language and gender preference | "Selasa pukul 10 nak ke klinik" (Tuesday 10am, clinic) → walk-with-me request, Tue 10:00, clinic | Yes (headline) | Read back \+ confirm; matching itself is **rule-based**, not AI |
| **G**: Give back | Write the helper's **impact story card** from completed sessions (template \+ LLM wording) | "8 walks with Mr Tan since Sept" | Yes (simple) | Facts come from the database only; no invented claims |
| Tanya Dulu (future) | Highlight scam red flags in a pasted message or screenshot | "Asks for OTP, claims to be police, urgent tone → be careful" | No — future release | If built later, **always** forwarded to a trusted human too; never says "safe" |
| Coordinator | Weekly digest: missed check-ins, unmatched requests, concern flags | "3 concern flags this week; 2 requests unmatched on Wed mornings" | Yes (simple) | De-identified where possible |

**Where AI is deliberately not used:**

- Choosing helpers (rule-based and explainable)  
- Inferring health or emotion  
- Certifying safety  
- Any external messaging channel. The MVP is app-only; if WhatsApp is added in Phase 2, Meta's ban on general-purpose AI chatbots means it stays buttons and reminders.

### Model choice

- **Primary (demo and early pilot): a Gemini Flash-class model** (e.g. *Gemini 3.8 Flash*, Sep 2026; \~US\$0.75 per 1M input tokens / US\$3.75 per 1M output).  
  - One API handles **audio \+ text** in, structured JSON out, and pairs with Google TTS for read-aloud.  
  - Cost is tiny at pilot scale: 50 elders × 5 voice requests/day × \~1k tokens ≈ 7.5M tokens/month ≈ **under US\$10/month**.  
  - Fits the Firebase/Vertex AI stack the team knows from GDGoC.  
- **Production candidate: ILMU (YTL AI Labs)**.  
  - Trained on **Malaysian-accented speech, Manglish and dialects**, which is the exact voice problem.  
  - **Hosted in Malaysia**, which eases PDPA cross-border rules.  
  - Closed API: request access and benchmark it against Gemini.  
- **On-device:** ML Kit only where needed (e.g. blurring faces in the Phase 2 photo reports).

### How we prove it works (Evidence based)

- **Voice test set:** record 30–50 requests from real elders (BM, EN, 中文, mixed) during W2 interviews, with consent.  
  - Metric: % of requests with all fields (activity, day, time, task) correct **after one read-back**. Target **≥85%**.  
- **Concern-flag test:** 40 sample check-in replies (half neutral, half with concern words).  
  - Target recall **≥90%**. Missing a concern is worse than a false flag.  
- **Future Tanya Dulu evaluation (outside the current MVP):** 20 real scam messages (from PDRM/MCMC awareness material) \+ 20 normal messages.
  - If the feature is built later, report precision and recall, and position it as "be careful", never "safe".
- **Phase 2 photo triage benchmark:** Project Sidewalk AI reached 81.3% precision / 77.2% recall.

## Open questions & risks, with prevention

| \# | Risk / open question | Sev. | What research says | Prevention / mitigation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| R1 | **Safeguarding incident** (abuse, theft, exploitation by a helper). Rewards raise the risk by attracting people motivated only by coins | High | Papa (US): dozens of harassment/assault allegations across 1.6m+ visits; insurers dropped it. Malaysia has no public background-check database; police clearance via PDRM/MyEG takes \~1–2 weeks | **Tiered helpers** (T1 phone → T2 public space with police clearance → T3 regular); number anonymisation; prominent emergency button; ID via SDP resident verification; training; **public-space-first** (meet at door or park, no home entry in pilot); check-in/out per session; block/report; named coordinator; two-person rule for door knocks |
| R2 | **"Home alone" data leaks** → burglary or scam targeting | High | PDPA treats health as sensitive; amended Act adds breach notification, DPO, fines up to RM1m | Never store or display "alone" as an attribute; helpers see task \+ meeting point only; role-based access \+ audit log; data minimisation; SDP as data controller with a named DPO |
| R3 | **Elders reject check-ins as surveillance** | High | FPF 2026: look-ins feel like surveillance; \~79% reject caregivers consenting for them | Elder-owned consent and settings; daily status only (no location, camera or content); "pause today" button; position it as "Saya OK", not "monitoring" |
| R4 | **Not enough weekday helpers** | Medium (was High) | Large national pools: ≈3.08m homemakers, ≈2.87m in schooling/training, ≈2.9m aged 65+; KampungKakis struggled with volunteer time; Nanjing intention–action gap | Invite people who are home in the daytime with the revised per-completion rewards; availability census to target recruitment; recurring small commitments (2 × 1 hr/week); group activities (1 helper : 3–4 elders at tai chi); weekend reciprocity; honest "no helper available" with coordinator fallback |
| R5 | **Coins crowd out goodwill**, feel like underpayment, or attract coin-farmers | Medium | Motivation crowding ("pay enough or don't pay at all", Gneezy & Rustichini 2000); Nanjing: personal growth was the strongest motive | Verify eligible completion and beneficiaries; deduplicate rewards by underlying event and participant; configure agreed rates on the backend; retain factual impact and recognition; test the revised model with elders and helpers |
| R6 | **Alert fatigue / false alarms** from missed check-ins | Medium | Iwate system worked by pairing automated check-ins with human follow-up | Elder-chosen windows; reminder before escalation; "away today" pre-set; tune thresholds in pilot; track false-alarm rate |
| R7 | **AI mishears a voice request or misses a concern word** (and, in Phase 2, misclassifies barriers) | Medium | Code-switching is hard for general models; Project Sidewalk photo AI \~81% precision | Always read back \+ confirm; concern flags tuned for high recall; buttons remain the primary path; benchmark Gemini vs ILMU; publish accuracy |
| R8 | **Reports go nowhere** (SDP doesn't own most public paths) | Medium | After handover, councils maintain roads and walkways | Owner field per asset; SISPAA prefill; monthly digest to SDP and council; show status honestly |
| R9 | **Liability & insurance** for helper injuries or incidents | Medium | No national volunteer accident scheme found; SOCSO SKSPS covers registered gig workers (see R21) | Group personal-accident policy via SDP/YSD, or SKSPS if helpers are classified as gig workers; partner NGO umbrella (e.g. MPKSM); waiver \+ clear task boundaries |
| R10 | **Cross-border data** to a foreign AI API | Medium | PDPA s129 \+ 2025 Guidelines: equivalent protection or exceptions; Transfer Impact Assessment | Redact before sending; no names or addresses to the AI; consent notice; evaluate Malaysia-hosted ILMU; do a TIA |
| R11 | **EmasCare becomes a scam vector** (fake helpers) | Medium | Elderly bear 27.9% of fraud losses | Verified identities only; helpers can't initiate contact outside the app; "never ask for money/OTP" rule in UI; helper report/block. Tanya Dulu is a future addition. |
| R12 | **Digital literacy**, especially elders who won't open a new app | Medium | 92.3% of 60+ use the internet, but app habits are WhatsApp-centred | Simple mode \+ voice; family-assisted onboarding; **phone-buddy call fallback**; KRT smartphone classes; WhatsApp channel in Phase 2 if pilot data shows need |
| R13 | **Cultural and gender norms** (e.g. Muslim women preferring female companions) | Medium | Malaysian multi-ethnic context | Gender preference in matching; same-language matching; respect prayer times in the calendar |
| R14 | **Dependency / loss of roles** | Low | Daytime-alone elders lose IADL roles (Uehara 2018\) | Design for contribution: elders as helpers, teachers, garden keepers |
| R15 | **Not an emergency service**, but people may treat it as one | Medium | n/a | Clear consent copy; 999 always visible; no medical claims |
| R16 | **SDP business case unclear** (who pays the coordinator?) | Medium | SDP strategy shifting to recurring income (malls); app has a voucher wallet | Show value to SDP: app engagement, mall footfall from voucher redemption, ESG "S" metrics, buyer appeal of multigenerational homes; pilot cost estimate below |
| R17 | Youth helpers (15–17) | Medium | Safeguarding complexity | **Exclude from pilot**; revisit with NGO partner |
| R18 | Senior Citizens Bill (expected early 2027\) may add duties | Low | Draft ready; tabling delayed | Monitor; design already rights-based |
| R19 | **WhatsApp policy** (Phase 2 only): Meta bans general-purpose AI chatbots on the Business Platform (from 15 Jan 2026\) | Low | Task-specific bots (bookings, reminders, support) allowed | WhatsApp stays structured (buttons, reminders); voice AI only in the SDP App; human hand-off |
| R20 | **Gamification backfires**: guilt from broken streaks, competition, or helping feeling transactional | Medium | Badges show no effect for already-motivated volunteers; gamification helps engagement but health effects are mixed | No streak penalties, no leaderboards, no points for check-ins; impact stories over badges; collective goals |
| R21 | **Rewarded-helper classification** under the revised per-completion model | Medium | The earlier monthly-appreciation reasoning is superseded; it does not establish the classification of the revised design | Review the revised reward model before a real pilot; do not rely on the previous flat-monthly rationale. The current build uses synthetic demo coins/vouchers |
| R22 | **Coins treated as regulated e-money** | Medium | BNM: limited-purpose exemption for "e-money for storing rewards" subject to conditions; open-loop or purchasable value needs approval | Earned-only, closed-loop (SDP malls \+ participating merchants), non-cashable, household-only transfer, expiry; confirm with BNM/lawyer |
| R23 | **Availability data reveals who is home** | Medium | Same burglary/scam risk as "home alone" status | Aggregate heatmaps only (cell ≥5); never show individual schedules; helpers see only their own matches |

### Pilot cost sketch (assumptions, to confirm with SDP)

| Item | Estimate (12 weeks) | Note |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Part-time community coordinator | \~RM6,000 | \~RM2,000/month, assumption |
| Helper police clearance (T2+, \~25 people) | Fee per clearance unconfirmed; pay via MyEG | n/a |
| Group personal-accident insurance | Quote needed | n/a |
| EmasCare Coins (voucher value) | To estimate after reward rates and eligibility are agreed | Model eligible completions × eligible participants × agreed coin value and expected redemption; the former monthly-helper estimate is superseded |

## Riskiest assumptions to prove before the finale

These are the assumptions that would sink EmasCare if wrong, ranked by **impact × uncertainty**. Each has a cheap test that can run before 14 Nov.

| Rank | Assumption | Type | Test (by date) | Pass if… |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **1** | Daytime-alone elders **want** company or outings, not just quiet | Desirability | Interview ≥5 daytime-alone elders (by 28 Oct): "Last weekday, where did you want to go but didn't?" | ≥3 of 5 describe an unmet outing or company need |
| **2** | Elders **accept a daily check-in** they control (not seen as surveillance) | Desirability | Show the check-in mock to elders and families separately; ask both "who should see what?" | ≥4 of 5 elders accept with their own settings; families accept "daily status only" |
| **3** | Working children **worry enough to act**: book help, install the module, help on weekends | Desirability / viability | Quick survey of ≥30 working adults with a parent at home (UM/GDGoC networks) \+ 5 interviews | ≥50% would use it; ≥30% would help ≥2 hrs/month on weekends |
| **4** | Enough residents are **free on weekday daytime** and would commit to a **regular weekly pairing** (≈2 hrs/week) with the revised activity/help rewards | Feasibility | **Daytime Availability Survey** (n≥50: Elmina/Subang community groups \+ UM students) by 28 Oct: free windows, role, willingness, reward preference | ≥30% free ≥2 hrs on weekdays AND willing; clear peak windows identified |
| 4b | Per-completion coins motivate participation by elders and helpers without crowding out goodwill; SDP-mall vouchers are attractive | Desirability | Test eligible action types, reward preferences and proposed rates with both roles; compare coins, recognition and participation without coins | Choose rates and eligibility from feedback; validate interest in SDP-mall vouchers before a pilot |
| **5** | Elders **trust a vetted neighbour they haven't met** | Desirability | Interview question \+ reaction to the helper profile card | Majority trust with conditions we can meet (SDP-verified, police clearance, same language/gender) |
| **6** | **SDP sees business value** and can integrate into its app | Viability | Mentor session: pilot interest, app module path, coordinator funding | Mentor confirms a plausible path, or names a blocker we can address |
| **7** | AI barrier triage is **accurate enough** to save staff time (Phase 2\) | Feasibility | Labelled 100-photo test (by 4 Nov) | ≥80% category accuracy; high-severity precision ≥0.8 |
| **8** | **Voice AI understands real elders** (mixed languages, accents) | Feasibility | Record 30–50 requests in W2 interviews; test in W3 | ≥85% fully correct after one read-back |
| 8b | Elders will **use the SDP App simple mode** (with family setup), or accept a phone-buddy call instead | Desirability / feasibility | W3 usability test with 3 elders: complete check-in \+ booking unaided after family setup | ≥2 of 3 complete both tasks; the rest accept the phone-buddy fallback |
| 9 | Light gamification (outing goal \+ family cheer) **motivates rather than pressures** | Desirability | Show the outing ring \+ cheer mock in W3 usability tests | Elders describe it as encouraging; no one reports guilt or pressure |
| 10 | Route-status data **stays fresh** (Phase 2\) | Feasibility | Can't be proven before the finale. Pilot metric: % of routes verified in last 14 days | Pilot target ≥80% |

**Already supported by secondary research (state confidently):**

- The group exists (74% co-residence; 69% female LFPR in Selangor)  
- The risks are real (falls, scams, poor social support)  
- Elders are online (92.3%)  
- Daily check-in \+ human follow-up works in Japan (Iwate)

**Weakest evidence (prioritise):** the Malaysian living-arrangement data is from **2009**. Look for newer data in the MARS (SWRC UM) or LPPKN Population & Family Survey tables.

## Delivery plan

### MVP scope (hackathon demo)

| In | Out (later or never) |
| :---- | :---- |
| Daily check-in ("Saya OK") with escalation to the family if missed | Wearables, cameras, live tracking |
| Weekday activity calendar (park tai chi, PAWE, surau/temple talks, garden, mall walk) | Event ticketing |
| Family (adult child) view: book help, see check-in and completion, with the parent's consent | Remote monitoring dashboards |
| Place/access problem reports and helper report/block to the coordinator | **Tanya Dulu** suspicious-call/message questions and scam-checking AI; any payments in the app |
| **Everything inside the SDP App module** (elder simple mode, family view, helper mode) \+ coordinator web dashboard | WhatsApp / SMS channels, WhatsApp mock (Phase 2\) |
| **Access notes** on \~5 activity places (icons, photo, walk time, toilet) \+ coordinator-set live status with auto-expiry \+ "Open in Google Maps" | Map engine, route planning, whole-township mapping |
| Simple accessibility filter on activities ("step-free only") | Mobility-profile routing, indoor navigation |
| "Report a problem" button (text/photo to coordinator, no AI); coordinator sets route status | AI photo triage, walk & report, owner routing (Phase 2\) |
| Request help: walk-with-me, sit-with-me, phone help, carry light item | Personal care, driving, home entry |
| Helper sign-up with availability census, tier badge, check-in/out, rating, block/report | Background checks API |
| **Teman voice assistant**: voice → check-in reply / booking, with read-back | Scam-question voice intent (future Tanya Dulu); open-ended AI chat companion |
| Light gamification: outing goal ring, family cheer, helper impact cards \+ coins, township collective goal | Levels, XP, leaderboards, avatars, tradable tokens |
| Elder/helper coin wallets: eligible verified completion → configured coin credit → accumulate → redeem a mock Elmina Lakeside Mall voucher | Real merchant settlement, coin purchase/cash-out, household transfers/donations/expiry, cash payments for tasks, open job feed |
| Availability heatmap (aggregate) on the coordinator dashboard | Predictive staffing |
| BM \+ EN UI; large-text mode; screen-reader labels | Full 中文/Tamil (show roadmap) |
| Optional mascot guide toggle | Pet help, transport (deep-link to GrabAssist only) |

### Future feature: Tanya Dulu (not in the current MVP)

A later release may let elders ask a trusted person about a suspicious call or message, with AI highlighting possible red flags and a human helping them decide what to do. Do not build its home action, question inbox, scam-question voice intent, or scam-checking AI integration in the current MVP or prototype. Revisit it after the core check-in, activity, companionship, and appreciation journeys are working and validated.

### Pilot KPIs

- Weekday outings per elder per week, before and after (**primary**)  
- Hours per weekday with someone or at an activity  
- Check-in completion rate; minutes from a missed check-in to contact; false-alarm rate  
- Family "peace of mind at work" (1–5), before and after  
- UCLA 3-item loneliness score, before and after (with consent)  
- Requests matched within the window (%); completion rate  
- Helper 8-week retention by pool (students / homemakers / retirees); weekend sign-ups by working children; elders who also help  
- Supply–demand overlap from the availability heatmap (% of requested slots with ≥1 available helper)  
- % of pairings kept each month; average pairing length (months)  
- Coins issued vs redeemed; % redeemed at SDP malls; merchant co-funding share  
- Access notes: accuracy on spot-checks; time to update a live status  
- SDP: module MAU, voucher redemptions at SDP malls

### Pitch storyline

1. "At 8am, Mr Tan's son leaves for KL. Until 7pm, the ground-floor room SDP designed for him is the only place he goes."  
2. Data: 74% vs 6%; 69% female LFPR; *nicchū dokkyo*; 1 in 7 falls; 27.9% of scam losses.  
3. Gap table (Existing solutions and the gap).  
4. SIANG framework \+ live demo (Flow A): Mr Tan *speaks* his booking to Teman, does the check-in, and completes an outing with Kak Lina. Verified completion updates progress and credits eligible participants at the agreed rates; his son sends a cheer, and a participant with sufficient coins redeems a mock voucher.
5. Evidence: interview quotes \+ survey numbers \+ AI accuracy.  
6. Why SDP: Value Multiplier; app module; mall vouchers; multigenerational buyers.  
7. Pilot: Elmina, 12 weeks, KPIs, cost; scale to 26 townships; Phase 2 adds full route mapping \+ OSM export.  
8. Safeguards and privacy (answer R1–R3 before judges ask).
